issues.legal_issue: When a founder dedicates a family residence to a family deity and appoints trustees to hold and use it for worship, but does not dispose of the shebaitship, the shebaitship devolves on the founder’s heirs under Hindu law.
material_facts: The founder made two wills that dealt with his properties in different territories and were read together by the Court.

One will dedicated the family residence to the family deity and directed the trustees to hold and use it for the deity’s service and worship, but did not expressly appoint them as shebaits or confer on them the role of managing or serving the deity.
The other will provided for the founder’s family and relatives to reside in the family residence; the founder’s descendants continued to live there and act as ministrants of the deity.
The defendant was a grandson of the founder and had occupied the disputed rooms.
issues.conclusion: The founder left the shebaitship undisposed of, so it devolved on his descendants under the ordinary rules of Hindu law. The defendant was a co-shebait and was entitled to reside in the disputed rooms.
issues.legal_principle: Property dedicated to an idol vests in the idol in an ideal sense, while the shebait acts as its human representative and custodian. Shebaitship combines office and property and is heritable; if the founder does not dispose of it, it devolves on the founder’s heirs under Hindu law unless a different usage or custom is shown. The Court applied Gossamee Shree Greedhareejee v. Rumanlaljee and considered Doorganath Roy v. Ram Chunder Sen and Pramatha Nath Mullick v. Pradyumna Kumar Mullick. It construed the two wills together and held that directions to hold and use property for worship, without more, created or described the endowment but did not dispose of shebaitship.

predicates.private_family_endowment: The founder set property apart for worship of a family deity rather than for public use.
predicates.will_does_not_dispose_of_shebaitship: The founder’s testamentary directions did not expressly or by necessary implication appoint the trustees as shebaits or otherwise dispose of the shebaitship.
predicates.wills_support_family_residence: The founder’s testamentary directions, read together, contemplated that the founder’s family and descendants would reside in the endowed family home.
predicates.founder_descendants_act_as_deity_ministr: The founder’s descendants living in the endowed home performed acts connected with the deity’s daily worship.

issues.definition: When a private family endowment is created but the founder does not dispose of shebaitship, the founder’s heirs inherit that shebaitship, particularly where the testamentary directions support family residence or the descendants act as ministrants.

issues.legal_issue: A shebait may validly relinquish shebaiti rights in favour of a co-shebait, including where the relinquishing shebait is not a descendant of the founder.
material_facts: The Court considered, alternatively, the possibility that the trustees had originally been constituted as shebaits.
Trustees who were not descendants of the founder did not act as shebaits and had ceased to participate in the matter.
The trustees accepted an arbitration award that treated the founder’s heirs and descendants as the persons entitled to act as shebaits, and the plaintiffs later described the defendant as a shebait.
issues.conclusion: Even if the trustees had originally been shebaits, the non-family trustees had relinquished any shebaiti rights in favour of the founder’s descendant co-shebaits, and that relinquishment was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Although shebaitship is not ordinarily freely transferable, a relinquishment in favour of a co-shebait may be valid. The Court relied on Nirod Mohini v. Shibdas, Mancharan v. Pranshankar, and Radhu Nath v. Purnanand, including the principle that a shebait seeking to give up the office may surrender it to the remaining shebaits.

rule.if: private_family_endowment and trustees_were_shebaits and non_family_shebaits_relinquished_rights and recipients_were_co_shebaits

predicates.private_family_endowment: The property was endowed for worship of a family deity.
predicates.trustees_were_shebaits: The persons appointed as trustees had also been constituted as shebaits of the deity.
predicates.non_family_shebaits_relinquished_rights: Trustees who were not members or descendants of the founder gave up any shebaiti rights they held.
predicates.recipients_were_co_shebaits: The persons in whose favour the rights were relinquished were co-shebaits of the deity.

issues.definition: Where trustees of a private family endowment were also shebaits, a non-family trustee’s relinquishment of shebaiti rights to co-shebaits is valid.

issues.legal_issue: Trustees cannot maintain a suit on behalf of an idol to recover endowed property when the right to sue belongs to the shebaits and not all shebaits are joined.
material_facts: The trustees brought a suit seeking possession of rooms in property dedicated to a family deity.
The legal title to the endowed property vested in the deity, not in the trustees.
The descendants of the founder were the shebaits, but not all of them were joined in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The trustees alone had no right to maintain the suit on behalf of the deity; because all the shebaits had not been joined, the suit was improperly constituted and liable to dismissal.
issues.legal_principle: Legal title to property dedicated to an idol vests in the idol, while the right to sue on the idol’s behalf vests in its shebaits. Where all the shebaits have not been made parties, a suit concerning the endowed property is not properly constituted.

rule.if: suit_seeks_possession_of_endowed_property and plaintiffs_sue_as_trustees_for_deity and shebaits_hold_right_to_sue and not all_shebaits_are_parties

predicates.suit_seeks_possession_of_endowed_propert: The proceeding is a suit seeking possession of property dedicated to an idol.
predicates.plaintiffs_sue_as_trustees_for_deity: The plaintiffs bring the suit in their capacity as trustees and seek relief on behalf of the deity.
predicates.shebaits_hold_right_to_sue: The right to sue on behalf of the deity belongs to its shebaits.
predicates.all_shebaits_are_parties: Every shebait of the deity has been joined as a party to the suit.

issues.definition: A suit by trustees seeking possession of endowed property on behalf of a deity is improperly constituted when the shebaits hold the right to sue and not all of them are parties.
